items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: Stan Getz was my guy you know.

ctx.x: I’m cracking up because if you look over my shoulder, I don’t know if you can tell but that’s Cannonball Adderley and he’s been my guy. And I saw him actually in Rochester a number of times. I mean it’s not the only person I listen to but for me he had everything I wanted from a saxophone player.
Yeah. Well there’s nothing wrong with that. Stan Getz was my guy you know.

I wanted to ask you about some of the other Legos that you’ve been able to construct and — arranging and composing — can you tell me where, first of all let’s talk about arranging. If you got a commission or you heard a tune that you wanted to arrange, let’s say for jazz ensemble, how do you go about thinking of a different way to set it so that you’re not just producing the original recording? Where do those thoughts come from?
